title: Saying Each Other with hverandre
goal: Use hverandre to describe actions shared between two or more people.

objectives.statement: Use hverandre to describe actions shared between two or more people.

sections.title: An evening at the community center

spans.value: Mina and Jonas help organize activities at a neighborhood community center. This evening, several volunteers are preparing a room for a language café.
Skal vi flytte bordene hver for oss?

blocks.translation: Should we move the tables separately?

spans.value: Nei, vi kan hjelpe hverandre.

blocks.translation: No, we can help each other.

spans.value: God idé. Sara og Emil snakker med hverandre om maten.

blocks.translation: Good idea. Sara and Emil are talking to each other about the food.

spans.value: Ja, og de nye frivillige kjenner ikke hverandre ennå.

blocks.translation: Yes, and the new volunteers do not know each other yet.

spans.value: Da kan vi presentere dem for hverandre.

blocks.translation: Then we can introduce them to each other.

spans.value: Perfekt. Etterpå sender vi hverandre en melding om neste uke.

blocks.translation: Perfect. Afterwards, we’ll send each other a message about next week.

spans.value: Everyone in the scene is doing something in relation to someone else. Mina helps Jonas, and Jonas helps Mina. Sara speaks to Emil, and Emil speaks to Sara. This shared, two-way relationship is expressed with
hverandre
, meaning
each other
or
one another
Use
hverandre
when two or more people perform an action that connects them reciprocally. A reciprocal action goes in both or several directions.

en.value: Mina and Jonas help each other.

spans.value: This means Mina helps Jonas and Jonas helps Mina.

no.value: Sara og Emil snakker med hverandre.

en.value: Sara and Emil talk to each other.

spans.value: Sara talks to Emil, and Emil talks to Sara.
The people involved normally appear together as the subject:

en.value: We understand each other.
They know each other well.
The teacher and the student respect each other.

spans.value: The subject may be a plural pronoun such as
vi
or
de
, or it may name two or more people.
Compact rule
Use
hverandre
when two or more participants do something to, for, with, or in relation to one another.
Hverandre
does not change for gender or number:

no.value: De to søstrene ringer hverandre hver søndag.

en.value: The two sisters call each other every Sunday.

no.value: De tre naboene hjelper hverandre om vinteren.

en.value: The three neighbors help one another in winter.

no.value: Vi møter hverandre ofte på bussen.

en.value: We often meet each other on the bus.

sections.title: Hverandre as the object of a verb

spans.value: Many verbs can take
hverandre
directly as their object. In these examples, no preposition is needed.

en.value: We help each other.
They know each other.
The children walk each other home.
The colleagues support each other.

no.value: Mina og Jonas møter hverandre ved inngangen.

en.value: Mina and Jonas meet each other at the entrance.

spans.value: Compare a sentence with a single-direction object:

en.value: Mina helps Jonas.

spans.value: Only Mina is presented as the helper. Jonas receives the help.
Now compare the reciprocal sentence:

en.value: Mina and Jonas help each other.

spans.value: Here the help goes both ways.
The same contrast appears with pronouns:

en.value: They help them.
They help each other.

spans.value: In the first sentence,
de
and
dem
may refer to two different groups. In the second, the members of the subject group help one another.
Common mistake: using an ordinary object pronoun
An English speaker may try to translate
each other
with a plural object pronoun:

no.value: Vi ser oss selv i speilet.

en.value: 'Not: We see ourselves in the mirror. (for the reciprocal meaning)'

spans.value: This has a reflexive meaning: we see ourselves. It does not express
we see each other
. Use
hverandre
for the reciprocal meaning:

en.value: We see each other every morning.

spans.value: Likewise:

en.value: They visit them often.

spans.value: This means one group visits another group. It does not say that the members visit one another.

en.value: They visit each other often.

spans.value: This clearly gives the reciprocal meaning.
Some actions connect people through a preposition. Norwegian keeps the preposition before
hverandre
In the opening dialogue, Sara and Emil were discussing the food:

no.value: Sara og Emil snakker med hverandre.

en.value: Sara and Emil talk to each other.

spans.value: The verb expression is
snakke med
, so the reciprocal expression is
med hverandre

en.value: We learn from each other.
They look after each other.
The neighbors share tools with each other.
The students practice with each other.

no.value: Mina og Jonas venter på hverandre utenfor.

en.value: Mina and Jonas wait for each other outside.

spans.value: The relevant preposition comes from the Norwegian expression:
Do not automatically copy the English preposition. Use the preposition required by the Norwegian verb or expression.
Compare:

en.value: They talk about each other.
They talk to each other.

spans.value: Both sentences contain
hverandre
, but the preposition changes the relationship. In the first, the people are the topic of conversation. In the second, they are conversation partners.
The central grammar point remains the same:
hverandre
identifies the people as reciprocally connected. The preposition tells us what kind of connection the verb requires.
The most important choice is not grammatical shape but meaning. Ask whether the action is presented as mutual.

en.value: Jonas sends Mina a message.

spans.value: This describes one message from Jonas to Mina.

no.value: Jonas og Mina sender hverandre meldinger.

en.value: Jonas and Mina send each other messages.

spans.value: This describes messages moving between them.

no.value: Sara presenterer Emil for de nye frivillige.

en.value: Sara introduces Emil to the new volunteers.

spans.value: Sara performs the introduction.

no.value: Sara presenterer de nye frivillige for hverandre.

en.value: Sara introduces the new volunteers to each other.

spans.value: Sara causes the new volunteers to become acquainted with one another.
A plural subject alone does not guarantee a reciprocal meaning:

en.value: Mina and Jonas open the door.

spans.value: They may perform the same action together, but they do not open one another. There is no reciprocal relationship.

no.value: Mina og Jonas ser på hverandre.

en.value: Mina and Jonas look at each other.

spans.value: Here each person looks at the other, so
hverandre
is appropriate.
Common mistake: treating every shared activity as reciprocal
People can do the same activity together without acting toward one another.

en.value: We make dinner together.
We make dinner for each other.

spans.value: This describes cooperation in one activity.
This says that each person makes food for the other.

en.value: They walk to work together.

no.value: De venter på hverandre før de går til jobben.

en.value: They wait for each other before walking to work.

spans.value: Use
hverandre
only when the action connects the participants in the intended reciprocal relationship.
English often uses
each other
for two people and sometimes
one another
for a larger group. Norwegian normally uses
hverandre
in both cases.

no.value: De to vennene stoler på hverandre.

en.value: The two friends trust each other.

no.value: Alle i gruppa lytter til hverandre.

en.value: Everyone in the group listens to one another.
The players encourage one another before the match.

no.value: Vi sender hverandre bilder fra turen.

en.value: We send one another pictures from the trip.

spans.value: With a larger group, the exact pattern of individual actions may depend on context. The sentence presents the group members as mutually connected; it does not always claim that every person performs the action separately toward every other person.
A practical way to form a reciprocal sentence is to start with the participants and the relationship.
First, combine the participants into a plural subject:

en.value: Mina and Jonas

spans.value: Then choose the action:

en.value: Mina and Jonas help

spans.value: Finally, add
hverandre

en.value: Mina and Jonas help each other.

spans.value: If the Norwegian expression needs a preposition, keep it:

no.value: Sara og Emil snakker med hverandre.

en.value: Sara and Emil talk to each other.

spans.value: Time and place information can make the sentence more useful:

no.value: Sara og Emil snakker med hverandre etter møtet.

en.value: Sara and Emil talk to each other after the meeting.

no.value: Vi hjelper hverandre når det er travelt.

en.value: We help each other when it is busy.
They call each other every Friday.

spans.value: The extra information changes the situation, but
hverandre
continues to express the same reciprocal relationship.
The room is ready, and the language café has begun.
De nye frivillige snakker med hverandre nå.

blocks.translation: The new volunteers are talking to each other now.

spans.value: Ja, og de hjelper hverandre med navnene.

blocks.translation: Yes, and they are helping each other with the names.

spans.value: Før kjente de ikke hverandre, men nå ler de sammen.

blocks.translation: Before, they did not know each other, but now they are laughing together.

spans.value: Det er bra. Vi lærer mye av hverandre her.

blocks.translation: That’s good. We learn a lot from one another here.

spans.value: Notice the contrast in Mina’s comment.
Kjenne hverandre
expresses a reciprocal relationship: the volunteers did not know one another.
Le sammen
describes a shared activity: they are laughing together. The sentence uses each expression for its own meaning.

sections.title: Guided transfer to a new situation

spans.value: Imagine three neighbors in an apartment building. During winter, they clear snow, share equipment, and check that everyone is safe. This setting gives several natural reasons to describe reciprocal actions.

en.value: The neighbors help one another with the snow.
They borrow tools from each other.

no.value: De passer på hverandre når det er glatt.

en.value: They look after one another when it is slippery.

no.value: Før snakket de nesten aldri med hverandre.

en.value: Before, they hardly ever talked to each other.

spans.value: The situation has changed, but the grammar has not. A plural group performs actions that connect its members in two or more directions.
Without looking back, recall what
hverandre
means and when it is appropriate. Then complete a short written review based on friends planning a weekend trip.

prompt.value: Choose the interpretation that shows a reciprocal relationship and identifies the participants connected by the action.

options.text: En frivillig hjelper lederen med forberedelsene. / One volunteer helps the leader with the preparations; connected participants: the volunteer and the leader.
options.why: The action goes from one volunteer to one leader, so it is not reciprocal.

options.text: De frivillige hjelper hverandre med forberedelsene. / The volunteers help one another with the preparations; connected participants: the volunteers.
options.why: The volunteers act toward one another, so the relationship is reciprocal.

prompt.value: Complete each Norwegian sentence with the reciprocal object form. In every sentence, the volunteers act toward one another.

spans.value: De frivillige hjelper
i sentrum. De frivillige møter
etter møtet. De frivillige kjenner
godt. De frivillige støtter
under forberedelsene. De frivillige kontakter
senere.

prompt.value: Rewrite the two Norwegian statements as one natural Norwegian sentence. Use De as the plural subject, the supplied verb expression, and hverandre. Maria snakker med Jonas. Jonas snakker med Maria.

explanation.value: Hverandre expresses participants acting on one another and follows any required preposition.

prompt.value: Classify each Norwegian sentence into exactly one bucket: a joint activity or a reciprocal action.

explanation.value: Doing something together is a joint action; hverandre is reserved for participants directing the action toward one another.

buckets.label: Joint activity: participants act together, not toward one another.
Reciprocal action: participants act toward one another.

items.text: Kollegaene reiser sammen. / The colleagues travel together.
Vennene lager mat sammen. / The friends cook together.
Søsknene studerer sammen. / The siblings study together.
Naboene hjelper hverandre med snøen. / The neighbors help one another with the snow.

prompt.value: Combine the two Norwegian statements into one natural Norwegian sentence. Use Mina og Jonas as the plural subject and hverandre; do not repeat the names as separate objects. Mina hjelper Jonas. Jonas hjelper Mina.

Write three complete Norwegian sentences about neighbors in a new everyday setting, not the community center. Use these cues: 1. The neighbors help one another after a storm. Use hjelpe. 2. They send messages containing information about icy paths to one another. Use sende meldinger til. 3. Last week, they borrowed tools from one another. Use låne verktøy av. Use hverandre directly where the verb takes a direct object and after the required preposition in the other expressions.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the response against the task and report evidence for each criterion. Accept natural Bokmål variants that preserve reciprocal meaning and the required prepositions.

criteria.instruction: Uses hverandre to describe reciprocal actions between two or more neighbors in the new setting.
Uses hverandre directly with hjelpe and after the required prepositions in sende meldinger til and låne verktøy av.

prompt.value: Write four concise Norwegian sentences from these English cues about friends planning a weekend trip: 1. The friends call one another to coordinate departure. 2. They wait for one another at the station. 3. They help one another with packing. 4. They send messages to one another while planning. Use hverandre only when the action is reciprocal. Include at least one verb that takes hverandre directly and at least one expression with a preposition before hverandre.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the response against the task and report evidence for each criterion. Accept natural Bokmål variants that preserve the intended reciprocal meanings.

criteria.instruction: Uses hverandre accurately only for reciprocal actions among two or more friends.
Includes at least one direct-object use of hverandre and at least one preposition plus hverandre construction.
Writes one complete Norwegian sentence for each of the four weekend-trip cues.
